`openacr validate` passes on the exact YAML above (pinned `@openacr/openacr@0.3.8`).

### Finish surface

You review the **YAML plus the rendered HTML directly**, as the audit plan specified. Do not route this draft through the GSA ACR Editor: it cannot import WCAG 2.2 documents today — it rejects them criterion by criterion. Edits go into the YAML; re-validate after each change. No out-of-catalog annex is needed here, because the draft uses the 2.2 catalog that matches the evaluation's conformance target — nothing measured falls outside it.

### The draft is incomplete — two Level AA criteria carry no term

This is deliberate and it is the reason the report is marked INCOMPLETE. An adherence term on either of these would be an overclaim, and the OpenACR tooling would not have stopped us: `openacr validate` passes on documents with missing criteria and even accepts `not-evaluated` on Level A criteria, which the catalog's own definition forbids. ### Two toolchain notes worth carrying forward

- **`openacr output` silently truncates without `-c`.** Rendering with only `-f` and `-t` produces a metadata-only page — every chapter and criterion dropped — while still printing "Valid and output generated". I reproduced this against the package's own reference document (Drupal 10: 159 KB as shipped, 14 KB when re-rendered without `-c`). The correct invocation passes the catalog explicitly: `openacr output -f draft.yaml -c node_modules/@openacr/openacr/catalog/2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en.yaml -t <template> -o draft.html`. Anyone re-rendering this file needs that flag or they will review a document with no findings in it and conclude everything is fine.
- **The AAA criterion list in the source brief was one short.** It named 30 criteria while stating 31; `3.3.9 Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)` was missing. I built the chapter from the pinned catalog rather than the prose list, so all 31 are present. Worth correcting in the audit plan template so the next engagement doesn't inherit the gap.
